chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Bashir al-Nabbal, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever emancipates a righteous soul for the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah will expiate from him, in place of every organ of his, an organ from the Fire.'

key_terms.عُضْو: Organ/limb — each bodily member finds its counterpart expiated from hellfire
key_terms.كَفَّرَ: To expiate, to cover over sins, to provide atonement
key_terms.لِوَجْهِ اللَّه: For the Face of God — sincere action done solely for God's pleasure
key_terms.نَسَمَة: A living soul/being, used here to denote an enslaved person

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for freeing a righteous slave for the sake of Allah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that freeing a righteous enslaved person — when done purely for God's sake — earns divine expiation proportional to every limb of one's body. In the early Islamic era, slavery was an established social institution, and the act of manumission (itq) was considered among the highest moral and spiritual deeds. The imagery of organ-for-organ atonement from hellfire underscores the profound spiritual merit of liberating a virtuous person.
